partialSkips.reason: Scored by exit code rather than by the marker it prints, because the marker is not the end of the run. The file is 1195 lines of Buffer assertions; at :1076 one branch wants a sha1 digest, common.hasCrypto is false on oam (it is Boolean(process.versions.openssl), common/index.js:54 -- see test-process-versions above for why oam publishes no openssl key), and the else branch calls common.printSkipMessage('missing crypto'), which writes '1..0 # Skipped: missing crypto' and does NOT exit (common/index.js:548). Execution continues through the remaining ~120 lines and the module body runs to completion. Measured on this machine: oam exits 0, the body reaches its end, and with the assert module's exported predicates instrumented 10352 assertion calls execute (a floor -- bare assert(...) calls route through the callable itself and are not counted). Exactly one comparison, the crypto digest, stands down. Treating the marker as authoritative booked all of that as a skip and dropped ~1100 lines of real Buffer coverage out of the denominator. See the _doc above for why this is a per-test opt-in and cannot be inferred from output: test-stream-pipeline-http2.js prints the identical line, also exits 0, and asserts nothing.

deliberateFailures.reason: A V8-VERSION divergence, not an oam gap -- the only entry here that is about the engine underneath oam rather than about oam. The test reads internalBinding('util').arrayBufferViewHasBuffer (V8's ArrayBufferView::HasBuffer: whether the view's backing ArrayBuffer OBJECT has been materialized yet) and asserts a table that is a V8 12 implementation detail -- expectOnHeap true, i.e. hasBuffer FALSE, at lengths 0 and 48, and hasBuffer TRUE at 96 and 1024, for Uint8Array / Uint16Array / Uint32Array / Float32Array / Float64Array / Buffer.alloc / Buffer.allocUnsafeSlow alike. Measured on this machine: real node v22.22.2 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.39) reproduces that table exactly and exits 0; oam links V8 15.0.245.2, which no longer allocates small typed arrays on the V8 heap, so every live ArrayBufferView genuinely HAS a buffer and the op answers true at all four lengths -- oam fails on the first case ('mismatch: false vs true for Uint8Array, length = 0'). oam's op (crates/oam_engine/src/node_ops.rs, op_array_buffer_view_has_buffer) is a wrapper over v8::ArrayBufferView::has_buffer() and reports the linked V8's answer faithfully: it is CORRECT, and it is the test's expectation that has expired. Passing would mean answering false for a buffer that demonstrably exists -- inventing a heap layout this V8 does not have -- and it would then contradict the test's own consistency check two lines further on, which reads .buffer and asserts hasBuffer is now true. Nothing in oam should change to chase it, and the test comes back by itself if V8 ever reintroduces on-heap typed arrays. Recorded as divergence 31 in docs/node-divergences.md. FOR REVIEW: this entry is why maxDeliberate moved 2 -> 3.

Asserts all 24 legacy process.binding names are truthy. oam models the ones it can back with the REAL implementation (constants, util, tty_wrap.isTTY) taken by identity off the public surface, and THROWS for the rest -- mostly libuv handle classes (TCP, UDP, Pipe, JSStream, FSEvent) it has nothing behind. Returning {} would claim them, and it is also worse for the caller than throwing: a package that feature-detects process.binding('tcp_wrap'), gets an empty object and proceeds hits a TypeError deep in its own code, where the throw sends it straight to the fallback branch that is correct for oam. See js/node_compat.js (process.binding).

Asserts a strict deep-equal on the process.versions KEY SET -- an ARRAY compare, so both membership and order are load-bearing. After common/index.js gates the optional groups, what the test still demands of oam is 'acorn', 'ares', 'cjs_module_lexer', 'llhttp', 'nbytes', 'nghttp2', 'simdjson', 'simdutf', 'uv', 'uvwasi', 'zlib', 'zstd' plus Node's own ABI counters 'modules' and 'napi' -- C libraries oam does not link and version numbers for an ABI it does not implement. It does NOT demand 'openssl'/'ncrypto', 'icu'/'cldr'/'tz'/'unicode', 'sqlite', 'ngtcp2'/'nghttp3', 'undici' or 'amaro': each of those groups suppresses its own requirement, because the test appends them only behind a common/index.js predicate derived from the very surface oam omits (index.js:54 hasCrypto = Boolean(process.versions.openssl); index.js:37 hasIntl = !!process.config.variables.v8_enable_i18n_support; hasSQLite, hasQuic, hasUndici and hasAmaro the same way). The compare also fails in the other direction, which is the part that cannot be fixed by adding keys: oam publishes the dependency tree it ACTUALLY builds against, generated from Cargo.lock at build time (v8, tokio, hickory, rustls, ring, oxc, hyper, brotli, flate2, icu, url, ada, h2, reqwest, unicode), and every one of those beyond the four the sets share -- 'node', 'v8', 'brotli', 'ada' -- is an extra key the deep-equal rejects. Passing would mean deleting the real names and inventing the absent ones, i.e. having process.versions state something false about the binary. The honest surface is worth more than the test.
